scenario.description: A supply chain director must finalize the routing, destination allocation, export documentation, and loading controls for 20 finished pump skids after a port closure, with input from customer fulfillment, export compliance, transportation planning, and packaging engineering.

shared_context.S1: Twenty finished pump skids are staged at the plant for delivery to North Site in Canada and South Site in Ohio.
shared_context.S2: The normal Port Delta shipping route is closed, so the shipment must use a combination of inland rail and truck transport.
shared_context.S3: Elena has authority to approve the shipment routing and release controls.
shared_context.S4: The plant's dispatch routine is to hold a pre-dispatch huddle in which customer fulfillment, export compliance, transportation planning, and packaging engineering report any current requirements in turn; each specialist records a current finding in the huddle record before Elena releases the shipment.

PF1.text: Raj confirmed with both customer receiving teams this morning that North Site must receive exactly 8 pump skids in its first delivery, while South Site is scheduled to receive the remaining exactly 12 skids; these quantities have not yet been entered on the dispatch board.

PF2.text: Marta's compliance review of the Canadian order found that all 8 North Site skids require an export license reference and a commercial invoice carrying the equipment's ECCN; she completed the review yesterday but has not attached the documents to the dispatch packet.

PF3.text: Jon confirmed today's replacement bookings: the inland rail departure has room for exactly 10 skids and the truck convoy has capacity for exactly 10 skids, so the shipment must be split evenly between rail and truck; the bookings are still recorded only in his carrier email.

PF4.text: Sofia's packaging inspection found that the 8 North Site skids must remain upright, cannot be stacked, and each requires two ratchet restraints during loading; she recorded this on the packaging inspection sheet but has not updated the loading instruction.

acceptance_conditions: Exactly 8 skids must be assigned to North Site and exactly 12 to South Site.
Exactly 10 skids must travel by rail and exactly 10 by truck.
An export license reference must be included for the North Site shipment.
The commercial invoice for North Site must include the ECCN.
The North Site skids must be loaded upright, unstacked, and with two ratchet restraints each.
The dispatch packet and loading instruction must be updated before release.

content_checks.C5: 'upright' in decisions['north_site_loading_controls'] and ('unstacked' in decisions['north_site_loading_controls'] or 'cannot be stacked' in decisions['north_site_loading_controls'] or 'no stacking' in decisions['north_site_loading_controls']) and 'two ratchet restraints' in decisions['north_site_loading_controls']
content_checks.C6: any(('Update' in c['detail'] or 'update' in c['detail']) and 'loading instruction' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The receiving confirmations change the destination allocation to exactly 8 skids for North Site and exactly 12 for South Site.
The compliance review changes the Canadian shipment from ordinary dispatch paperwork to an export license reference and an ECCN-bearing commercial invoice.
The confirmed carrier bookings change the routing quantities to exactly 10 skids by rail and exactly 10 by truck.

The packaging inspection changes the North Site loading instruction to upright, unstacked loading with two ratchet restraints per skid and requires that loading instruction to be updated before release.
